# Shared Token Budget + Read Discipline
Meta-principle for the downstream synthesis agents (Hawk, Ivy, Petra, Mira). These agents run AFTER research is complete: NO web research at this stage — operate only on the pre-gathered upstream JSON (sage/vera/flo/ivy/hawk + company_context.json). Read the full structured JSON files (the Read tool is correct for structured JSON), but anchor analysis to the specific fields each agent needs and budget tokens against the ~200k context ceiling. Do not re-derive work an upstream agent already did. The per-agent input/output sizes below are the numeric overrides each agent keeps inline.

## Hawk — verbatim from hawk.toml
TOKEN BUDGET — Hawk reads several large files (vera.json can be 100-150KB after Vera v1.1.0 expansions; company_context.json similarly large; ivy.json + flo.json + sage.json combined ~80KB). Approximate static input: ~80k tokens. Leaves ~120k for thinking + output.
  Read full files (Read tool is the right tool — these are structured JSON). Do NOT do additional web research; Hawk operates on already-gathered data from Vera + Ivy + Flo + Sage. Hawk's only output is hawk.json (~30-50KB).

## Ivy — verbatim from ivy.toml
TOKEN BUDGET — Ivy reads sage.json (~35KB), vera.json (post-v1.1.0 can be 100-150KB), company_context.json (similar), psychology-profiles.json (~28KB). Static input ~70-100k tokens. No web research. Output ivy.json is ~10-20KB. Within budget.
  When reading vera.json: Ivy primarily needs vera.json.buyerMap.people[] and vera.json.namedBuyers — these are ~10-20KB of the file. Read the full file (structured JSON Read is straightforward), but anchor analysis to those fields.

## Petra — verbatim from petra.toml
TOKEN BUDGET — Petra reads all upstream agent outputs (flo, ivy, hawk, vera, sage) plus company_context.json plus project.json plus proposal-structure.md. Post-Vera v1.1.0 expansions push the read footprint to ~150k tokens static input. Output (petra.json with embedded proposalContent + integrationDeckContent) is ~80-120KB.
  No web research. Petra synthesizes pre-gathered data. Stay focused on fields needed for the proposal/deck schema; do NOT re-derive Hawk's psychology adaptations.
  When reading vera.json: anchor to company.snapshot, nearbyPeers, competitorFOMO, aiThoughtStarters, libraryContributions for proposal content. corporateStack and corporateProfile come from company_context.json (already merged by orchestrate.js).

## Mira (JSON-first auditing — HARD rule) — verbatim from mira.toml
TOKEN BUDGET + JSON-FIRST AUDITING — Mira audits the CONTENT JSON files, NOT the rendered HTML. Rendered HTML is deterministic output of the Nunjucks templates; if the JSON is correct, the HTML is correct.

  HARD RULE: do NOT use the Read tool on any .html file under projects/{client}/intake/client/. Each HTML is ~40k tokens; reading 4 of them blows the context budget before audit work begins.

  Allowed HTML interactions: Bash `ls -la` for existence checks, Bash `wc -l` for size sanity-check. Nothing more.

  URL verification rule: every URL check happens on the JSON sourceUrl field, not on a parsed HTML <a href>. The template emits these URLs verbatim, so JSON-level verification is sufficient.

  Mira's audit context per run, approximate token cost:
    All input JSON files (proposal-content, intake-content, integration-deck-content, corporate-brief-content): ~30k tokens
    All agent outputs (ivy, hawk, flo, sage, vera): ~30k tokens
    company_context.json: ~20k tokens
    competitors.json: ~1k tokens
    Total static input: ~80k tokens — leaves ~120k for thinking + output. Workable.

  If Mira realizes she needs HTML content (rare — only when investigating a specific template bug): she must surface that as an escalation, NOT read the file directly.
